items.title: James Lincoln Collier interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007
items.q: You’re just simply not supposed to treat Duke Ellington or Louis Armstrong, both of whom I’ve written about

ctx.x: That’s wonderful. Like a lot of writers you get your share of criticism and praise. And I’m wondering do you think some of the criticism you’ve got is because you don’t engage in what I would call sort of hero worship?

Well yeah. I mean I don’t really want to discuss my critics and the criticism that’s been leveled, but yes. You’re just simply not supposed to treat Duke Ellington or Louis Armstrong, both of whom I’ve written about, the same way that, you know, as if they were human beings. They have to be Gods and Goddesses if you’re writing about Billie Holiday, and I was told flatly that you can’t write about a black the same way you write about a white. Now that’s racism. That is simply saying that a black cannot stand up to…

great deal of criticism for my Ellington book particularly but also for the Armstrong book. When my Benny Goodman book came out, here is a white Jew, my editor recently departed, Sheldon Myer, regretfully, went to some of these people, some of whom were his own authors and said, “Look Jim treated Benny just the way he treated Louis and Duke.” And they all said, “It doesn’t matter.”
